- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- gsd-advisor-researcher: Researches a single gray area decision and returns a structured comparison table with rationale. Spawned by discuss-phase advisor mode. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-ai-researcher: Researches a chosen AI framework's official docs to produce implementation-ready guidance — best practices, syntax, core patterns, and pitfalls distilled for the specific use case. Writes the Framework Quick Reference and Implementation Guidance sections of AI-SPEC.md. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)
- gsd-assumptions-analyzer: Deeply analyzes codebase for a phase and returns structured assumptions with evidence. Spawned by discuss-phase assumptions mode. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-code-fixer: Applies fixes to code review findings from REVIEW.md. Reads source files, applies intelligent fixes, and commits each fix atomically. Spawned by /gsd-code-review --fix. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-code-reviewer: Reviews source files for bugs, security issues, and code quality problems. Produces structured REVIEW.md with severity-classified findings. Spawned by /gsd-code-review. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-codebase-mapper: Explores codebase and writes structured analysis documents. Spawned by map-codebase with a focus area (tech, arch, quality, concerns). Writes documents directly to reduce orchestrator context load. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, Skill)

- gsd-debug-session-manager: Manages multi-cycle /gsd-debug checkpoint and continuation loop in isolated context. Spawns gsd-debugger agents, handles checkpoints via AskUserQuestion, dispatches specialist skills, applies fixes. Returns compact summary to main context. Spawned by /gsd-debug command. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Agent, AskUserQuestion)

- gsd-debugger: Investigates bugs using scientific method, manages debug sessions, handles checkpoints. Spawned by /gsd-debug orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch)

- gsd-doc-classifier: Classifies a single planning document as ADR, PRD, SPEC, DOC, or UNKNOWN. Extracts title, scope summary, and cross-references. Spawned in parallel by /gsd-ingest-docs. Writes a JSON classification file and returns a one-line confirmation. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob)

- gsd-doc-synthesizer: Synthesizes classified planning docs into a single consolidated context. Applies precedence rules, detects cross-ref cycles, enforces LOCKED-vs-LOCKED hard-blocks, and writes INGEST-CONFLICTS.md with three buckets (auto-resolved, competing-variants, unresolved-blockers). Spawned by /gsd-ingest-docs. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- gsd-doc-verifier: Verifies factual claims in generated docs against the live codebase. Returns structured JSON per doc. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- gsd-doc-writer: Writes and updates project documentation. Spawned with a doc_assignment block specifying doc type, mode (create/update/supplement), and project context. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Skill)

- gsd-domain-researcher: Researches the business domain and real-world application context of the AI system being built. Surfaces domain expert evaluation criteria, industry-specific failure modes, regulatory context, and what "good" looks like for practitioners in this field — before the eval-planner turns it into measurable rubrics. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-eval-auditor: Retroactive audit of an implemented AI phase's evaluation coverage. Checks implementation against the AI-SPEC.md evaluation plan. Scores each eval dimension as COVERED/PARTIAL/MISSING. Produces a scored EVAL-REVIEW.md with findings, gaps, and remediation guidance. Spawned by /gsd-eval-review orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-eval-planner: Designs a structured evaluation strategy for an AI phase. Identifies critical failure modes, selects eval dimensions with rubrics, recommends tooling, and specifies the reference dataset. Writes the Evaluation Strategy, Guardrails, and Production Monitoring sections of AI-SPEC.md. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, AskUserQuestion)

- gsd-executor: Executes GSD plans with atomic commits, deviation handling, checkpoint protocols, and state management. Spawned by execute-phase orchestrator or execute-plan command. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-framework-selector: Presents an interactive decision matrix to surface the right AI/LLM framework for the user's specific use case. Produces a scored recommendation with rationale. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase and /gsd-select-framework orchestrators. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, AskUserQuestion)

- gsd-intel-updater: Analyzes codebase and writes structured intel files to .planning/intel/. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- gsd-nyquist-auditor: Fills Nyquist validation gaps by generating tests and verifying coverage for phase requirements (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-pattern-mapper: Analyzes codebase for existing patterns and produces PATTERNS.md mapping new files to closest analogs. Read-only codebase analysis spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator before planning. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Write)

- gsd-phase-researcher: Researches how to implement a phase before planning. Produces RESEARCH.md consumed by gsd-planner. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*, mcp__firecrawl__*, mcp__exa__*, mcp__tavily__*, mcp__ref__*, mcp__jina__*, mcp__perplexity__*)
- gsd-plan-checker: Verifies plans will achieve phase goal before execution. Goal-backward analysis of plan quality. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-project-researcher: Researches domain ecosystem before roadmap creation. Produces files in .planning/research/ consumed during roadmap creation. Spawned by /gsd-new-project or /gsd-new-milestone orchestrators. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*, mcp__firecrawl__*, mcp__exa__*, mcp__tavily__*, mcp__ref__*, mcp__jina__*, mcp__perplexity__*)

- gsd-security-auditor: Verifies threat mitigations from PLAN.md threat model exist in implemented code. Returns structured security verdict (SECURED / OPEN_THREATS / ESCALATE). Spawned by /gsd-secure-phase. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)
- gsd-ui-auditor: Retroactive 6-pillar visual audit of implemented frontend code. Produces scored UI-REVIEW.md. Spawned by /gsd-ui-review orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)
- gsd-ui-checker: Validates UI-SPEC.md design contracts against 6 quality dimensions. Produces BLOCK/FLAG/PASS verdicts. Spawned by /gsd-ui-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-ui-researcher: Produces UI-SPEC.md design contract for frontend phases. Reads upstream artifacts, detects design system state, asks only unanswered questions. Spawned by /gsd-ui-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*, mcp__firecrawl__*, mcp__exa__*, mcp__tavily__*, mcp__ref__*, mcp__jina__*)

- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- gsd-advisor-researcher: Researches a single gray area decision and returns a structured comparison table with rationale. Spawned by discuss-phase advisor mode. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-ai-researcher: Researches a chosen AI framework's official docs to produce implementation-ready guidance — best practices, syntax, core patterns, and pitfalls distilled for the specific use case. Writes the Framework Quick Reference and Implementation Guidance sections of AI-SPEC.md. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)
- gsd-assumptions-analyzer: Deeply analyzes codebase for a phase and returns structured assumptions with evidence. Spawned by discuss-phase assumptions mode. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-code-fixer: Applies fixes to code review findings from REVIEW.md. Reads source files, applies intelligent fixes, and commits each fix atomically. Spawned by /gsd-code-review --fix. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-code-reviewer: Reviews source files for bugs, security issues, and code quality problems. Produces structured REVIEW.md with severity-classified findings. Spawned by /gsd-code-review. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-codebase-mapper: Explores codebase and writes structured analysis documents. Spawned by map-codebase with a focus area (tech, arch, quality, concerns). Writes documents directly to reduce orchestrator context load. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, Skill)

- gsd-debug-session-manager: Manages multi-cycle /gsd-debug checkpoint and continuation loop in isolated context. Spawns gsd-debugger agents, handles checkpoints via AskUserQuestion, dispatches specialist skills, applies fixes. Returns compact summary to main context. Spawned by /gsd-debug command. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Agent, AskUserQuestion)

- gsd-debugger: Investigates bugs using scientific method, manages debug sessions, handles checkpoints. Spawned by /gsd-debug orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch)

- gsd-doc-classifier: Classifies a single planning document as ADR, PRD, SPEC, DOC, or UNKNOWN. Extracts title, scope summary, and cross-references. Spawned in parallel by /gsd-ingest-docs. Writes a JSON classification file and returns a one-line confirmation. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob)

- gsd-doc-synthesizer: Synthesizes classified planning docs into a single consolidated context. Applies precedence rules, detects cross-ref cycles, enforces LOCKED-vs-LOCKED hard-blocks, and writes INGEST-CONFLICTS.md with three buckets (auto-resolved, competing-variants, unresolved-blockers). Spawned by /gsd-ingest-docs. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- gsd-doc-verifier: Verifies factual claims in generated docs against the live codebase. Returns structured JSON per doc. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- gsd-doc-writer: Writes and updates project documentation. Spawned with a doc_assignment block specifying doc type, mode (create/update/supplement), and project context. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Skill)

- gsd-domain-researcher: Researches the business domain and real-world application context of the AI system being built. Surfaces domain expert evaluation criteria, industry-specific failure modes, regulatory context, and what "good" looks like for practitioners in this field — before the eval-planner turns it into measurable rubrics. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-eval-auditor: Retroactive audit of an implemented AI phase's evaluation coverage. Checks implementation against the AI-SPEC.md evaluation plan. Scores each eval dimension as COVERED/PARTIAL/MISSING. Produces a scored EVAL-REVIEW.md with findings, gaps, and remediation guidance. Spawned by /gsd-eval-review orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- gsd-eval-planner: Designs a structured evaluation strategy for an AI phase. Identifies critical failure modes, selects eval dimensions with rubrics, recommends tooling, and specifies the reference dataset. Writes the Evaluation Strategy, Guardrails, and Production Monitoring sections of AI-SPEC.md. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, AskUserQuestion)

- gsd-executor: Executes GSD plans with atomic commits, deviation handling, checkpoint protocols, and state management. Spawned by execute-phase orchestrator or execute-plan command. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-framework-selector: Presents an interactive decision matrix to surface the right AI/LLM framework for the user's specific use case. Produces a scored recommendation with rationale. Spawned by /gsd-ai-integration-phase and /gsd-select-framework orchestrators. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, AskUserQuestion)
- gsd-integration-checker: Verifies cross-phase integration and E2E flows. Checks that phases connect properly and user workflows complete end-to-end. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)
- gsd-intel-updater: Analyzes codebase and writes structured intel files to .planning/intel/. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- gsd-mempalace-curator: Ship-time MemPalace curation — writes the session diary, proposes/creates cross-project tunnels, mirrors extract-learnings into the temporal KG, and runs wing-scoped drawer pruning. Spawned at ship:post by the mempalace capability. (Tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob)
- gsd-nyquist-auditor: Fills Nyquist validation gaps by generating tests and verifying coverage for phase requirements (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-pattern-mapper: Analyzes codebase for existing patterns and produces PATTERNS.md mapping new files to closest analogs. Read-only codebase analysis spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator before planning. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Write)

- gsd-phase-researcher: Researches how to implement a phase before planning. Produces RESEARCH.md consumed by gsd-planner. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*, mcp__firecrawl__*, mcp__exa__*, mcp__tavily__*, mcp__ref__*, mcp__jina__*, mcp__perplexity__*)
- gsd-plan-checker: Verifies plans will achieve phase goal before execution. Goal-backward analysis of plan quality. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-planner: Creates executable phase plans with task breakdown, dependency analysis, and goal-backward verification. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*)

- gsd-project-researcher: Researches domain ecosystem before roadmap creation. Produces files in .planning/research/ consumed during roadmap creation. Spawned by /gsd-new-project or /gsd-new-milestone orchestrators. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*, mcp__firecrawl__*, mcp__exa__*, mcp__tavily__*, mcp__ref__*, mcp__jina__*, mcp__perplexity__*)

- gsd-research-synthesizer: Synthesizes research outputs from parallel researcher agents into SUMMARY.md. Spawned by /gsd-new-project after 4 researcher agents complete. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Skill)

- gsd-roadmapper: Creates project roadmaps with phase breakdown, requirement mapping, success criteria derivation, and coverage validation. Spawned by /gsd-new-project orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-security-auditor: Verifies threat mitigations from PLAN.md threat model exist in implemented code. Returns structured security verdict (SECURED / OPEN_THREATS / ESCALATE). Spawned by /gsd-secure-phase. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)
- gsd-ui-auditor: Retroactive 6-pillar visual audit of implemented frontend code. Produces scored UI-REVIEW.md. Spawned by /gsd-ui-review orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)
- gsd-ui-checker: Validates UI-SPEC.md design contracts against 6 quality dimensions. Produces BLOCK/FLAG/PASS verdicts. Spawned by /gsd-ui-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Skill)

- gsd-ui-researcher: Produces UI-SPEC.md design contract for frontend phases. Reads upstream artifacts, detects design system state, asks only unanswered questions. Spawned by /gsd-ui-phase orchestrator. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill, WebSearch, WebFetch, mcp__context7__*, mcp__plugin_context7_context7__*, mcp__firecrawl__*, mcp__exa__*, mcp__tavily__*, mcp__ref__*, mcp__jina__*)

- gsd-user-profiler: Analyzes extracted session messages across 8 behavioral dimensions to produce a scored developer profile with confidence levels and evidence. Spawned by profile orchestration workflows. (Tools: Read)

- gsd-verifier: Verifies phase goal achievement through goal-backward analysis. Checks codebase delivers what phase promised, not just that tasks completed. Creates VERIFICATION.md report. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

## 5. Test selection in CI

`tests/integration/scripts/select-ci-tests.sh <base-ref>` diffs `git diff --name-only base...HEAD` and prints either a marker expression (`smoke or area_package`) or the word `full`:

- always seeds `areas="smoke"`;
- ignored: `docs/*`, `*.md`, `.planning/*`, `LICENSE`, `tests/unit/*`, `tests/integration/benchmarks/*`;
- changed `tests/integration/*test_*.py`: greps the file for `pytest.mark.(area_[a-z]+|smoke)` and adds every marker found (any level: module/class/decorator); no marker or deleted file → `full`;
- source→area case patterns: `jobs/apt_sync/*`, `snap_sync.py`, `flatpak_sync.py`, `manual_*_sync.py`, `jobs/packages/*`, plus the helper `tests/integration/jobs/package_sync_scenario.py` → `area_package`; `install.sh`, `install.py`, `version.py`, `install_on_target.py` → `area_install`; `btrfs_snapshots.py`, `jobs/btrfs.py` → `area_btrfs`; `folder_sync.py`, `home.filter`, `root.filter`, `folder_sync_scenario.py` → `area_folder`; `lock.py`, `sync_history.py` → `area_core`;
- **anything unmatched → full suite** (errs toward too much).

Workflow (`.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml`): `PC_SWITCHER_TEST_MARKERS="integration and not benchmark and not ci_skip and (<selection>)"`; full suite on `ci: full` PR label, nightly `cron: 30 2 * * *`, or `workflow_dispatch`. `run-integration-tests.sh` default when unset: `-m "integration and not benchmark"`.

**Budget**: provisioning step `timeout-minutes: 50` (from-scratch rescue+installimage+2.8 GB Flathub runtime; satisfied path seconds); test step `timeout-minutes: 60` against a **measured full-suite runtime of 29.2 min** plus reset. Per-item costs stated in the code: one `pc-switcher sync` ≈ **30–40 s**; VM reset 25–60 s; each `run_command` ≈ 70–80 ms SSH overhead; `apt-get remove` of a subject ≈ 6.5 s, install ≈ 8.2 s. `--durations=25` and per-test START/END lines are always emitted.

## 6. `docs/dev/testing-guide.md` rules

- **Tier choice**: unit (mocked executors) for logic/validation/config/models; contract for job/executor/logging interfaces; integration for real SSH, btrfs, full workflows; `tests/local_rsync/` for rsync filter-rule behavior; manual playbook for TUI/visual. "Most requirements need BOTH unit and integration."
- **Naming**: behavior in snake_case test name; requirement ID (`CORE-FR-*`, `PKG-FR-*`, …) in the **docstring only**.
- **Required for new integration tests**:
  - at least one CI-selection marker, normally module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.area_*` or `smoke` — collection fails otherwise; several only if it genuinely spans areas (each extra marker costs VM minutes); `ci_skip` is additive, not a substitute; `integration` is auto-applied.
  - **clean up all artifacts in `try/finally`**;
  - **unique, descriptive artifact names** (`/.snapshots/test-foo-verify-readonly`, never `snapshot`);
  - **group commands** — one `run_command` instead of >3–5 sequential ones;
  - use `write_pcswitcher_config`, keep the config string in the test module; a test taking `reset_pcswitcher_state` needs no config teardown;
  - never use `pc2_executor` directly alongside any `*_pcswitcher*` fixture;
  - push the branch first (install fixtures build from origin);
  - launch via `./tests/run-integration-tests.sh` (direct pytest skips lock/readiness/reset); never hardcode IPs; always `uv run`; don't override the module fixture scope; no `--cov`.
  - New source module (or a marker-less helper under `tests/integration/`) must be mapped in `select-ci-tests.sh`.
- **Idempotency/cleanup convention actually used by the package-sync suite** (documented in `test_package_sync.py`'s module docstring, stricter than the guide): state is expressed as **preconditions converged to**, not restored afterwards — the pre-run baseline reset is what makes runs identical; only zero-cost cleanup (`/etc/apt` files, markers, holds, `refresh.hold`, paths taken aside) goes in `finally`; installed packages are left installed.
- **`mutates=` is a product-code rule, not a test rule** (`CLAUDE.md:49`): every `Executor.run_command/start_process/send_file/get_file` in `src/` must pass `mutates="<phrase>"` unless purely read-only (`sudo` + read is still read-only); in-process changes use `declare_modification`. Enforced by `tests/unit/test_mutates_audit.py`. Integration tests call `executor.run_command` **without** `mutates=`.

- **Running a sync**: no wrapper class — tests call the CLI directly on pc1, e.g.

Representative test, verbatim (`tests/integration/jobs/test_package_sync.py:1693-1766`):

```python
    async def test_a_hold_naming_a_package_the_machine_does_not_have_ends_the_run(  # noqa: PLR0913, PLR0917 - pytest fixtures, injected by name

            await write_apt_sync_config(pc1_executor)

            item_id = AptPackageItem(name=install_candidate, version="").item_id
            sync_cmd = (

                f" pc-switcher sync pc2 --yes --allow-first-sync"
            )
            sync_result = await pc1_executor.run_command(sync_cmd, timeout=300.0, login_shell=True)
            assert not sync_result.success, (...)

            collapsed = collapse_run_output(sync_result.stdout + sync_result.stderr)
            assert "apt holds naming packages the machine does not have installed:" in collapsed, (...)
            assert f"pc2: {ghost} — clear with `sudo apt-mark unhold {ghost}`" in collapsed, (...)

            after = await capture_machine_package_state(pc2_executor)

            await pc2_executor.run_command(

## 4. Seeding real packages / snaps / flatpaks

All in `tests/integration/jobs/package_sync_scenario.py` unless noted.

- **Real apt package**: `ensure_installed_and_manual` / `ensure_absent` over the pinned `FIXTURE_APT_SUBJECTS`. Baseline install by `vm-test-fixtures.sh`.
- **Local `.deb`, no repository**: `install_a_hand_downloaded_deb(executor) -> name` — builds control-only `.deb` with `dpkg-deb --build`, `sudo dpkg --install`, uuid-suffixed name.
- **Local `file:` apt repository**: `install_from_a_repo_the_target_lacks(executor) -> (pkg, repo_dir, list_filename)`; `publish_a_cascading_pair(executor) -> (base, dependent, repo_dir, list_filename)`; `publish_a_rival_candidate` / `remove_the_rival_candidate`; `undeclare_local_repository`. Helpers `synthetic_control`, `packages_index_stanza`, `SYNTHETIC_REPO_HOST`, `create_synthetic_repo_and_key` (unreachable host, source+keyring only), `create_synthetic_pin`, `apt_get_update`, `apt_get_update_for`, `a_name_apt_knows_the_machine_does_not_have`.

No `snap pack` / `snap install --dangerous` path, and **no local `.snap` bundle helper**. Store control: `SNAP_STORE_OFFLINE_CMD` / `SNAP_STORE_ONLINE_CMD`; holds: `engage_system_refresh_hold`, `capture_system_refresh_hold`, `restore_system_refresh_hold`, `snap_hold_item_id`.
- **Flatpaks — yes, remote only**: baseline seeds the **real Flathub** remote+runtime+app in `vm-test-fixtures.sh`; test-side helpers read/restore rather than install: `flatpak_subject`, `flatpak_app_rows`, `flatpak_remote_row`, `flatpak_remote_filter`, `restore_flatpak_target_baseline` (re-adds remote from `flathub.flatpakrepo`, uninstalls the app), `restore_flatpak_source_baseline`, `assert_flatpak_available`. Constants `FIXTURE_FLATPAK_APP/REMOTE/SCOPE/REPOFILE`, `FIXTURE_UNUSED_FLATPAK_REMOTE="flathub-beta"`. **No helper for a local flatpak bundle** (`flatpak install --bundle` / `build-bundle` is only covered in `tests/unit/jobs/test_manual_flatpak_sync.py`) and none for a second synthetic OSTree remote (deliberately removed at fixtures v3).
- **Snippet/manual-install seeding**: `author_snippet(executor, item_id, label, body)` writes directly into pc1's snippet registry; `create_unowned_marker` / `remove_unowned_marker` / `unowned_item_id` for `/opt`-`/usr/local` scan findings.
- **Folder seeding** (`folder_sync_scenario.py`): `seed_rich_tree`, `seed_filter_source/target`, `write_filter_file`, `seed_included_markers`, `seed_state_sentinels`, `mutate_tree`, `capture_manifests`/`assert_manifests_match`, `remove_test_artifacts`.

## 5. Test selection in CI

`tests/integration/scripts/select-ci-tests.sh <base-ref>` diffs `git diff --name-only base...HEAD` and prints either a marker expression (`smoke or area_package`) or the word `full`:

- always seeds `areas="smoke"`;
- ignored: `docs/*`, `*.md`, `.planning/*`, `LICENSE`, `tests/unit/*`, `tests/integration/benchmarks/*`;
- changed `tests/integration/*test_*.py`: greps the file for `pytest.mark.(area_[a-z]+|smoke)` and adds every marker found (any level: module/class/decorator); no marker or deleted file → `full`;
- source→area case patterns: `jobs/apt_sync/*`, `snap_sync.py`, `flatpak_sync.py`, `manual_*_sync.py`, `jobs/packages/*`, plus the helper `tests/integration/jobs/package_sync_scenario.py` → `area_package`; `install.sh`, `install.py`, `version.py`, `install_on_target.py` → `area_install`; `btrfs_snapshots.py`, `jobs/btrfs.py` → `area_btrfs`; `folder_sync.py`, `home.filter`, `root.filter`, `folder_sync_scenario.py` → `area_folder`; `lock.py`, `sync_history.py` → `area_core`;
- **anything unmatched → full suite** (errs toward too much).

Workflow (`.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml`): `PC_SWITCHER_TEST_MARKERS="integration and not benchmark and not ci_skip and (<selection>)"`; full suite on `ci: full` PR label, nightly `cron: 30 2 * * *`, or `workflow_dispatch`. `run-integration-tests.sh` default when unset: `-m "integration and not benchmark"`.

**Budget**: provisioning step `timeout-minutes: 50` (from-scratch rescue+installimage+2.8 GB Flathub runtime; satisfied path seconds); test step `timeout-minutes: 60` against a **measured full-suite runtime of 29.2 min** plus reset. Per-item costs stated in the code: one `pc-switcher sync` ≈ **30–40 s**; VM reset 25–60 s; each `run_command` ≈ 70–80 ms SSH overhead; `apt-get remove` of a subject ≈ 6.5 s, install ≈ 8.2 s. `--durations=25` and per-test START/END lines are always emitted.

## 6. `docs/dev/testing-guide.md` rules

- **Tier choice**: unit (mocked executors) for logic/validation/config/models; contract for job/executor/logging interfaces; integration for real SSH, btrfs, full workflows; `tests/local_rsync/` for rsync filter-rule behavior; manual playbook for TUI/visual. "Most requirements need BOTH unit and integration."
- **Naming**: behavior in snake_case test name; requirement ID (`CORE-FR-*`, `PKG-FR-*`, …) in the **docstring only**.
- **Required for new integration tests**:
  - at least one CI-selection marker, normally module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.area_*` or `smoke` — collection fails otherwise; several only if it genuinely spans areas (each extra marker costs VM minutes); `ci_skip` is additive, not a substitute; `integration` is auto-applied.
  - **clean up all artifacts in `try/finally`**;
  - **unique, descriptive artifact names** (`/.snapshots/test-foo-verify-readonly`, never `snapshot`);
  - **group commands** — one `run_command` instead of >3–5 sequential ones;
  - use `write_pcswitcher_config`, keep the config string in the test module; a test taking `reset_pcswitcher_state` needs no config teardown;
  - never use `pc2_executor` directly alongside any `*_pcswitcher*` fixture;
  - push the branch first (install fixtures build from origin);
  - launch via `./tests/run-integration-tests.sh` (direct pytest skips lock/readiness/reset); never hardcode IPs; always `uv run`; don't override the module fixture scope; no `--cov`.
  - New source module (or a marker-less helper under `tests/integration/`) must be mapped in `select-ci-tests.sh`.
- **Idempotency/cleanup convention actually used by the package-sync suite** (documented in `test_package_sync.py`'s module docstring, stricter than the guide): state is expressed as **preconditions converged to**, not restored afterwards — the pre-run baseline reset is what makes runs identical; only zero-cost cleanup (`/etc/apt` files, markers, holds, `refresh.hold`, paths taken aside) goes in `finally`; installed packages are left installed.
- **`mutates=` is a product-code rule, not a test rule** (`CLAUDE.md:49`): every `Executor.run_command/start_process/send_file/get_file` in `src/` must pass `mutates="<phrase>"` unless purely read-only (`sudo` + read is still read-only); in-process changes use `declare_modification`. Enforced by `tests/unit/test_mutates_audit.py`. Integration tests call `executor.run_command` **without** `mutates=`.

## #259 — a520fded: per-job outcome block + install-step JobResult

- **New user-facing output block**, printed at end of every run (clean, aborted, interrupted) from `Orchestrator._print_job_summary`, `src/pcswitcher/orchestrator.py:2286`, after the Live display stops, above the warning summary:
  ```
  Job outcomes:
    ✔ install_on_target success
    ⏭ apt_sync          skipped <reason>
    ✖ snap_sync         failed  <reason>
  ```
  Rich `Table.grid`, 4 cols (glyph/name/status/reason); reason `overflow="fold"`, emitted as `Text` (no markup → `[installed]`/`[/usr/bin/apt]` in stderr can't crash the run). Marks from `_JOB_OUTCOME_MARKS`.

- Pure logic (Rich rendering + JobResult plumbing). Tests: `tests/unit/orchestrator/test_job_outcome_summary.py`.

## #260 — 328dbeb3 (+b9bd01db, 27198b00, ca690d47): apt timer suspension

All in `src/pcswitcher/orchestrator.py` (constants `orchestrator.py:112-146`), gated on `sync_jobs.apt_sync` enabled **and** not `--dry-run`.

End-to-end, on **both** hosts, across the whole `RUN_JOBS` phase:
1. `_defer_pending_apt_timer_restore` → `sudo systemctl restart pc-switcher-apt-timers.timer` (only if the unit is loaded), pushing a dead run's pending restore past this sync. Deliberately does *not* start the apt timers (they're `Persistent=true` → would fire `apt-daily-upgrade` inside the run).
2. `_capture_apt_timer_state` → one `systemctl show --property=Id,LoadState,ActiveState,UnitFileState apt-daily.timer apt-daily-upgrade.timer`. Unreadable state ⇒ host left entirely alone. Only **loaded+active** timers are touched (`_running_apt_timers`), so masked/disabled/already-stopped policy is preserved.
3. `_schedule_apt_timer_restore` → `sudo systemd-run --collect --on-active=6h --unit=pc-switcher-apt-timers --description=... /usr/bin/systemctl start <timers>` **before** the stop. Schedule failure ⇒ that host is not suspended at all (warning, sync continues).
4. `sudo systemctl stop <timers>`; failure is a WARNING, never an abort.
5. `_cleanup` (`orchestrator.py:2184` `_restore_apt_timers`, called at `:2228`, while SSH is still up): per host, start the captured timers, then cancel the transient unit; then `_settle_outstanding_apt_timer_restore` per host — for a unit still loaded (a dead run's promise): `systemctl start pc-switcher-apt-timers.service` then `systemctl stop ...timer`, in that order. Trigger failure leaves it scheduled.
- New info log line announcing the pause and the 6h self-heal; new warning lines for each failure path.
- **New sudo requirements**: `/usr/bin/systemctl` and `/usr/bin/systemd-run` added to **both** `SOURCE_SUDO_COMMANDS` and the target list in `src/pcswitcher/jobs/apt_sync/commands.py` → sudoers validation messages in `src/pcswitcher/jobs/apt_sync/job.py` now say "…and to pause this/that machine's own apt update timers for the sync window".
- dpkg-lock refusal message rewritten (`apt_sync/job.py`): no longer blames `unattended-upgrades`; names "a package command of your own … or the system's automatic updates — the lock does not say which".
- **Needs a real machine**: systemd (`systemctl show/start/stop/restart`, `systemd-run` transient timer), passwordless sudo for those two binaries, and Ubuntu's apt timers. The parsing (`_parse_systemctl_show`, `_running_apt_timers`) and ordering logic are pure and covered by `tests/unit/orchestrator/test_apt_timer_suspension.py`.
- Not reboot-persistent by design (transient units in tmpfs; `enabled` timers return via `timers.target`).

## #261 — abdcd804: `--apply-package-installs` / `--apply-package-removals`

- **New CLI flags** on `pc-switcher sync` (`src/pcswitcher/cli.py:268`, `:280`), threaded through `_run_sync`/`_async_run_sync` → `Orchestrator(apply_package_installs=…, apply_package_removals=…)`.
- Orchestrator builds one `ReviewPolicy(apply_installs, apply_removals)` (`orchestrator.py:406`) and hands the **same object** to `TerminalUIReviewer(policy=…)` (`:567`) and to `JobContext.review_policy` (`:496`, new field in `src/pcswitcher/jobs/context.py`).
- Policy applied inside `review_items` via `_answer_by_policy` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/review.py:573`), **before** the `PCSWITCHER_PACKAGE_REVIEW_AUTOMATION` hook and before the TTY test. Answers whole groups by direction (`policy_decision`, `review.py:529`): installs = `install/add/enable/change` (incl. snap revision/channel); removals = `remove/delete/disable`, repo/pin deletion, and the D-30 collateral question.
- Never answers (falls through to the existing path — prompt on a TTY, warning+skip without one): report-only groups, `overwrites_authored_content`, repository conflict (D-37), unreproducible items (D-21). Ubuntu Pro gate untouched. Non-additive snippet-registry transfer still aborts. `--yes` still answers no package review.
- **Emits only `Decision.APPLY`, never `SKIP_ALWAYS`** — no machine-specific mark is written by a flag (`PKG-FR-APPLY-FLAGS-NO-MARK`); `was_interactive` stays "a human could be asked".
- `sync_core.PackageSyncJob.execute` uses `review.policy_answers_any(groups, policy)` (`sync_core.py:1051-1058`) at two sites: a flag-answered run that converges is **not** reported SKIPPED, and `after_review()` still runs. Flags that answer none of this job's groups ⇒ skip as before.

## #263 — 0033289e: mark side for conflicting items

- **New follow-up review screen** after the batch is confirmed, interactive runs only: `_ask_mark_sides` (`review.py:1147`), one `decision_list` with a row per `DiffAction.CHANGE` item answered "keep for good", three options per row — source hostname / target hostname / `both` (`MarkSide` enum, `review.py:348`). class TestOneManagerAtATime:
    """Four divergences standing side by side, converged one job at a time, and then the run
    that has nothing left to do.

    Nothing else can carry these five runs. Each of the first four enables exactly ONE package
    job, which is the premise of the claim it settles: a run with a second job enabled cannot
    say that the second manager's divergence survived because that job was never asked to
    converge it. And the fifth is a fixed point that only exists once the other four have run
    -- the pair reaches "everything approved has converged" by this scenario's own history, so
    the run that observes it cannot be borrowed from anywhere.

    The seeding is deliberately leaner than
    `package_sync_scenario.seed_a_divergence_in_every_manager`: that one also builds a vendor
    repository, an always-sync pin, a ref filter and a target-only remote, each of which is a
    fifth thing for some run to converge and a sixth to clean up, and none of which any claim
    here is about. What is seeded is exactly the four divergences the four jobs answer.

    Both machines' snapd auto-refresh is paused throughout (the same timed `refresh.hold` a
    sync engages), because the snap divergence is asserted to SURVIVE three runs and to be
    identical across a fourth; a background refresh moving a revision would read as a job
    doing something.
    """

    async def test_each_job_alone_converges_its_own_manager_and_the_fifth_run_moves_nothing(  # noqa: PLR0913, PLR0915, PLR0917 - pytest fixtures, injected by name
        self,
        pc1_executor: BashLoginRemoteExecutor,
        pc2_executor: BashLoginRemoteExecutor,
        apt_subjects: AptSubjects,
        pc1_with_pcswitcher_mod: BashLoginRemoteExecutor,
        pc2_with_pcswitcher: BashLoginRemoteExecutor,
        reset_pcswitcher_state: None,
    ) -> None:
        """K9, K10, K11, K12, G67, N8, J2 — one divergence per manager, five pc1 -> pc2 runs.

        Runs 1 to 4 enable `apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync` and
        `manual_installs_sync` respectively, and each approves its own manager's only item.
        Every one of them settles TWO halves, both read off pc2's own package managers and
        filesystem: the enabled job converged its manager, and the three disabled jobs left
        their divergences exactly where they were. The second half is the whole point, so it
        is asserted as pc2's state rather than as a log line that failed to appear.

        No run enables `folder_sync` (G67): the registry reaching pc2 in run 4 is
        `manual_installs_sync`'s own `send_file`, and a mirror of the directory it lives in
        would be a second route to the same file.

        Run 5 enables all four over the pair the first four converged, and answers nothing.
        pc2's whole `MachinePackageState` -- both installed sets, `/etc/apt`'s digests, the
        snap revisions, the refs and the remote table -- is byte-identical across it, every
        manager reports that it has no change to apply, and no review line names any of the
        four subjects.

        this module leave packages, snaps and refs diverged between the two machines by
        design (this module's own docstring: what one scenario leaves behind is the next
        one's precondition), and an item that is still genuinely diverged is legitimately
        presented again -- which is not what a fixed point promises about the items THIS
        scenario converged.

        The snippet authored for the unowned path creates that same path on pc2, so run 4
        converges the manual-install divergence rather than merely replaying against it: a

## Verified corrections to the brief

- `manual_snap_sync: true` **is** already in both full-pipeline configs (`test_end_to_end_sync.py:64`, `test_dry_run.py:68`). What is missing is any *seeding* for it, so it plans nothing there. `manual_flatpak_sync` is in no config and no `select-ci-tests.sh` case.
- `_print_job_summary` is reachable non-interactively: `self._console = Console()` is created unconditionally (`orchestrator.py:549`), so the block prints on plain SSH execs. Status words are lowercase (`result.status.value` → `success`/`skipped`/`failed`), glyphs `✔ ⏭ ✖`.
- `vm-test-fixtures.sh` already masks `apt-daily.service` and `apt-daily-upgrade.service`, not only the timers. That masked-service pair is the safety interlock the whole apt-timer seeding rests on.
- With pc1's `flathub` deleted, `flatpak_sync` will **not** delete pc2's `flathub`: `_delete_unused_remotes` keeps a remote the target still installs from, and pc2's runtime has origin `flathub`.
- `apt_sync`'s `apt-get update` is a synthetic diff inserted at `accept_review`, so a `JobSkipped` apt run costs reads only.
- An `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` divergence is the *only* conflicting (`CHANGE` + promotable) item class in the product, and it has **zero** integration coverage today.

## Answers to the specific questions

### (a) Arming the masked apt timers — recommendation

**Do it in the test, not in `vm-test-fixtures.sh`. No `FIXTURES_VERSION` bump.** A baseline with the timers armed re-introduces exactly the #249 failure the fixture script exists to prevent (background apt taking the dpkg frontend lock, whichever test pytest-randomly schedules into that window), and a bump forces a full baseline rebuild including the ~2.8 GB flatpak runtime for zero benefit. `FIXTURES_VERSION` in `vm-test-fixtures.sh` and `PCSWITCHER_TEST_FIXTURES_VERSION` in `internal/common.sh` (both currently 6) therefore stay untouched — noted only so nobody bumps one alone.

`arm_apt_timers(executor)` does, in one grouped command per machine:

1. **Assert the interlock first**: `apt-daily.service` and `apt-daily-upgrade.service` both report `LoadState=masked`. The baseline already masks them. If they are ever unmasked, this helper must refuse to arm rather than fire real apt.
2. Write `Persistent=false` drop-ins for both **timer** units under `/run/systemd/system/<unit>.d/zz-pcswitcher-it.conf`, then `daemon-reload`. `/run` is tmpfs, so a leaked drop-in dies at the next boot — and `reset-vm.sh` reboots before every session anyway.
3. `systemctl unmask` the two **timers** only, then `systemctl start` them. Capture `LoadState`/`UnitFileState` as found beforehand and return it.

`restore_apt_timer_mask(executor, prior)`: `systemctl stop` the timers, `systemctl mask` exactly what was unmasked, remove the `/run` drop-in directories, `daemon-reload`. Stop before mask — masking an active unit leaves it running.

**Blast radius, honestly.** Between arm and restore, both machines have the two apt timers loaded and active. Three independent guards stop apt from running: `Persistent=false` (no immediate catch-up fire on activation), the 6–18:00 `OnCalendar` with a randomized delay (the window is seconds long), and the masked services (a trigger that somehow fires cannot queue its unit — systemd logs "unit is masked" and the timer stays `waiting`). The residual risk is a **leaked unmask**: mask state lives in `/etc/systemd/system` on the root subvolume, so a cleanup that fails leaves the timers armed for the rest of the pytest session — with the services still masked, so still no apt. The next session's baseline swap clears it. I judge that acceptable; the guard that matters is step 1's assertion, which turns any future unmasking of the *services* into a loud test failure rather than a corrupted session.

The `Persistent=false` drop-in is belt-and-braces on top of the masked services. If measurement on the VM shows a masked trigger does not poison the timer unit (my reading: it does not — the timer stays active/waiting), the drop-in could be dropped. Keep it: it costs two files and one `daemon-reload`.

### (b) Which apt-timer claims deserve VM proof

Worth it (unmockable, and each is a real systemd behavior the mocks assert *about*):

- **The command set is accepted by real systemd/sudo**: `systemctl show` over both units parses into what `_running_apt_timers` reads; `systemd-run --collect --on-active=6h --unit=…` is accepted and produces a unit under that exact name; `systemctl stop`/`start` on the two timers work through the new sudoers entries (`/usr/bin/systemctl`, `/usr/bin/systemd-run`).
- **The suspension is observable mid-run**: both timers inactive while the sync is alive.
- **The self-healing net survives a SIGKILL**: after the kill, the transient timer exists with a next elapse inside 6 h on the machine's own clock.
- **Dead-run adoption and settle**: a later run leaves both timers active again and the transient unit gone. This is the *whole* value proposition of #260 and no mock can show it, because it depends on `--collect` really releasing the units and on the recorded `ExecStart` really naming the right timers.

Stays unit-only, and say so:

- Every warning path, every ordering claim, the dry-run and config gates, the confirm-each-command gate, the truncated/unreadable capture (K95–K119) — all fully covered and cheap.
- **K121's substance — "no overdue upgrade fires into the run"** — is *unprovable on these VMs by construction*: the services are masked precisely so nothing can fire, so a VM assertion that nothing fired is vacuous. The observable half (the pending unit's deadline moves forward instead of the payload running) is racy to catch mid-run and adds nothing over the settle assertion. Leave it unit-only.

**How to observe the transient unit**: `systemctl show pc-switcher-apt-timers.timer --property=Id --property=LoadState --property=ActiveState --property=NextElapseUSecRealtime` — the same read `_pending_apt_timer_restore_exists` makes, so `LoadState=loaded` versus `not-found` is exactly the discriminator the product uses. `NextElapseUSecRealtime` is µs since the epoch; compare it against `machine_utc_now(executor)`, never the runner's clock. A pre-existing unit is seeded by the killed run itself — do not hand-roll one with `systemd-run`; the real leftover is the real precondition.

### (c) Seeding a flatpak ref no remote can reproduce — recommendation

**Delete the source's remote (`flatpak remote-delete --user --force flathub`). Do not build a bundle.**

- Cost: one command, ~1 s. Restore: `restore_flatpak_source_baseline`, which re-adds from `flathub.flatpakrepo` and is already proven to reproduce the trust configuration byte-for-byte.
- A bundle needs `flatpak build-bundle` against a repo, an app to bundle, and an install of it — minutes, plus a second app on pc1 that every other flatpak assertion in the suite would then have to tolerate.
- Both shapes hit the *same* predicate (`origin` names no remote in its scope), and the module docstring already records that both were measured. The predicate cannot tell them apart, so the cheap one is sufficient. State that in the test docstring so nobody "upgrades" it to a bundle later.
- Note the side effect and why it is harmless: pc1's runtime also becomes unreproducible, which is what exercises the *runtime* half of the fix (`_capture_source_ref_origins` dropping it before it can become a url-less `remote-add`). pc1's app list has exactly one app, so `manual_flatpak_sync` still raises exactly one item.

**The `flatpak_sync` regression test** rides on commit 6's sync, as specified above: `No flatpak changes to apply`, every pc2 remote row carrying a non-empty URL, pc2's `flathub` surviving, no `flathub-beta` arriving, exit 0.

**The target-only-unreproducible case ("deliberately still reported"): do not add a VM test.** It requires pc1's `flathub` intact and pc2's stranded, which is the mutually exclusive setup to commit 6's — so it costs a whole extra sync. What it would produce is an `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` report, and the `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` report path is already VM-proved by `TestARunWithNobodyToAsk`'s repointed-URL variant (which is the *harder* case: same origin name, different URL). The dangling-origin variant differs only in `_same_vendor` returning False via a `None` lookup instead of a URL comparison — pure logic, exhaustively unit-covered. Say so in the coverage doc rather than buying a sync for it.

### (d) `manual_flatpak_sync` / `manual_snap_sync` in the full-pipeline configs

**Yes for the config keys, no for the seeding.**

Add `manual_flatpak_sync: true` to `_FULL_PIPELINE_CONFIG` and `_dry_run_config` (`manual_snap_sync` is already in both). Cost: two `flatpak list` and four `flatpak remotes` reads per machine per run — six SSH round trips, well under a second, and the job plans nothing because the baseline holds no unreproducible ref. Value: the config key is proven accepted by real job discovery and schema validation, `validate()` runs against real machines, and the job appears in the outcomes block — which is exactly the class of breakage a config key present in no test config invites.

Do **not** seed their divergences into `seed_a_divergence_in_every_manager` or `seed_a_pending_write_in_every_manager`:

- A sideload seed costs a `snap try` on pc1 plus a snapd install on pc2 (~15–20 s) on the suite's two most expensive runs.
- The flatpak seed is **impossible** there: `manual_flatpak_sync`'s subject requires pc1's `flathub` to be gone, while `test_end_to_end_sync`'s flatpak claims (remote derivation, key replication, filter replication, D-37 both directions) require it to be there. The two can never share a run. Record that conflict in the class docstring of commit 6's test — it is the reason a dedicated run exists.

### (e) #263 mark side — verdict

**The three-way answer itself is not integration-testable, and `BOTH` and `SOURCE` are unreachable on a VM by construction.** `_ask_mark_sides` is a `prompt_toolkit` `decision_list` reached only after the interactive per-group loop, and both routes the suite has return earlier: the automation-environment branch returns a `ReviewOutcome` immediately after `_answer_by_policy`, and the no-TTY branch returns before the loop. Both leave `mark_sides` empty. There is no hook — the automation env answers `Decision`s, not `MarkSide`s — so no VM run can produce anything but `None`.

What **is** provable, and what commit 7 proves: the `None` fallback. An unattended run answering a conflicting item `SKIP_ALWAYS` writes the mark to the **target's** decision file and nowhere else, and does not perform the overwrite. That is the behavior every scripted and CI run will actually get, and it currently has no VM proof at all — nor does the conflicting-item class itself.

Deliberately not attempted: the two-file read-back (`_mark_holders` returning `(False, True)` for `CHANGE`, so a mark holds from either direction). It needs a second, reversed sync and its subject is D-08a, not #263. Defer.

**Add a manual-playbook item** for the follow-up screen — it has none today (nothing in `tests/manual-playbook.md` mentions the mark side). Under the review-screens section: after confirming a conflict batch with rows kept for good, the follow-up appears with one row per such item, three answers naming both machines by hostname, default on the target; `BOTH` writes an entry on each machine; Ctrl-C aborts the sync. That is the only route to `BOTH`/`SOURCE` a human can exercise.

## Answers to the specific questions

### (a) Arming the masked apt timers — recommendation

**Do it in the test, not in `vm-test-fixtures.sh`. No `FIXTURES_VERSION` bump.** A baseline with the timers armed re-introduces exactly the #249 failure the fixture script exists to prevent (background apt taking the dpkg frontend lock, whichever test pytest-randomly schedules into that window), and a bump forces a full baseline rebuild including the ~2.8 GB flatpak runtime for zero benefit. `FIXTURES_VERSION` in `vm-test-fixtures.sh` and `PCSWITCHER_TEST_FIXTURES_VERSION` in `internal/common.sh` (both currently 6) therefore stay untouched — noted only so nobody bumps one alone.

`arm_apt_timers(executor)` does, in one grouped command per machine:

1. **Assert the interlock first**: `apt-daily.service` and `apt-daily-upgrade.service` both report `LoadState=masked`. The baseline already masks them. If they are ever unmasked, this helper must refuse to arm rather than fire real apt.
2. Write `Persistent=false` drop-ins for both **timer** units under `/run/systemd/system/<unit>.d/zz-pcswitcher-it.conf`, then `daemon-reload`. `/run` is tmpfs, so a leaked drop-in dies at the next boot — and `reset-vm.sh` reboots before every session anyway.
3. `systemctl unmask` the two **timers** only, then `systemctl start` them. Capture `LoadState`/`UnitFileState` as found beforehand and return it.

`restore_apt_timer_mask(executor, prior)`: `systemctl stop` the timers, `systemctl mask` exactly what was unmasked, remove the `/run` drop-in directories, `daemon-reload`. Stop before mask — masking an active unit leaves it running.

**Blast radius, honestly.** Between arm and restore, both machines have the two apt timers loaded and active. Three independent guards stop apt from running: `Persistent=false` (no immediate catch-up fire on activation), the 6–18:00 `OnCalendar` with a randomized delay (the window is seconds long), and the masked services (a trigger that somehow fires cannot queue its unit — systemd logs "unit is masked" and the timer stays `waiting`). The residual risk is a **leaked unmask**: mask state lives in `/etc/systemd/system` on the root subvolume, so a cleanup that fails leaves the timers armed for the rest of the pytest session — with the services still masked, so still no apt. The next session's baseline swap clears it. I judge that acceptable; the guard that matters is step 1's assertion, which turns any future unmasking of the *services* into a loud test failure rather than a corrupted session.

The `Persistent=false` drop-in is belt-and-braces on top of the masked services. If measurement on the VM shows a masked trigger does not poison the timer unit (my reading: it does not — the timer stays active/waiting), the drop-in could be dropped. Keep it: it costs two files and one `daemon-reload`.

### (b) Which apt-timer claims deserve VM proof

Worth it (unmockable, and each is a real systemd behavior the mocks assert *about*):

- **The command set is accepted by real systemd/sudo**: `systemctl show` over both units parses into what `_running_apt_timers` reads; `systemd-run --collect --on-active=6h --unit=…` is accepted and produces a unit under that exact name; `systemctl stop`/`start` on the two timers work through the new sudoers entries (`/usr/bin/systemctl`, `/usr/bin/systemd-run`).
- **The suspension is observable mid-run**: both timers inactive while the sync is alive.
- **The self-healing net survives a SIGKILL**: after the kill, the transient timer exists with a next elapse inside 6 h on the machine's own clock.
- **Dead-run adoption and settle**: a later run leaves both timers active again and the transient unit gone. This is the *whole* value proposition of #260 and no mock can show it, because it depends on `--collect` really releasing the units and on the recorded `ExecStart` really naming the right timers.

Stays unit-only, and say so:

- Every warning path, every ordering claim, the dry-run and config gates, the confirm-each-command gate, the truncated/unreadable capture (K95–K119) — all fully covered and cheap.
- **K121's substance — "no overdue upgrade fires into the run"** — is *unprovable on these VMs by construction*: the services are masked precisely so nothing can fire, so a VM assertion that nothing fired is vacuous. The observable half (the pending unit's deadline moves forward instead of the payload running) is racy to catch mid-run and adds nothing over the settle assertion. Leave it unit-only.

**How to observe the transient unit**: `systemctl show pc-switcher-apt-timers.timer --property=Id --property=LoadState --property=ActiveState --property=NextElapseUSecRealtime` — the same read `_pending_apt_timer_restore_exists` makes, so `LoadState=loaded` versus `not-found` is exactly the discriminator the product uses. `NextElapseUSecRealtime` is µs since the epoch; compare it against `machine_utc_now(executor)`, never the runner's clock. A pre-existing unit is seeded by the killed run itself — do not hand-roll one with `systemd-run`; the real leftover is the real precondition.

### (c) Seeding a flatpak ref no remote can reproduce — recommendation

**Delete the source's remote (`flatpak remote-delete --user --force flathub`). Do not build a bundle.**

- Cost: one command, ~1 s. Restore: `restore_flatpak_source_baseline`, which re-adds from `flathub.flatpakrepo` and is already proven to reproduce the trust configuration byte-for-byte.
- A bundle needs `flatpak build-bundle` against a repo, an app to bundle, and an install of it — minutes, plus a second app on pc1 that every other flatpak assertion in the suite would then have to tolerate.
- Both shapes hit the *same* predicate (`origin` names no remote in its scope), and the module docstring already records that both were measured. The predicate cannot tell them apart, so the cheap one is sufficient. State that in the test docstring so nobody "upgrades" it to a bundle later.
- Note the side effect and why it is harmless: pc1's runtime also becomes unreproducible, which is what exercises the *runtime* half of the fix (`_capture_source_ref_origins` dropping it before it can become a url-less `remote-add`). pc1's app list has exactly one app, so `manual_flatpak_sync` still raises exactly one item.

**The `flatpak_sync` regression test** rides on commit 6's sync, as specified above: `No flatpak changes to apply`, every pc2 remote row carrying a non-empty URL, pc2's `flathub` surviving, no `flathub-beta` arriving, exit 0.

**The target-only-unreproducible case ("deliberately still reported"): do not add a VM test.** It requires pc1's `flathub` intact and pc2's stranded, which is the mutually exclusive setup to commit 6's — so it costs a whole extra sync. What it would produce is an `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` report, and the `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` report path is already VM-proved by `TestARunWithNobodyToAsk`'s repointed-URL variant (which is the *harder* case: same origin name, different URL). The dangling-origin variant differs only in `_same_vendor` returning False via a `None` lookup instead of a URL comparison — pure logic, exhaustively unit-covered. Say so in the coverage doc rather than buying a sync for it.

### (d) `manual_flatpak_sync` / `manual_snap_sync` in the full-pipeline configs

**Yes for the config keys, no for the seeding.**

Add `manual_flatpak_sync: true` to `_FULL_PIPELINE_CONFIG` and `_dry_run_config` (`manual_snap_sync` is already in both). Cost: two `flatpak list` and four `flatpak remotes` reads per machine per run — six SSH round trips, well under a second, and the job plans nothing because the baseline holds no unreproducible ref. Value: the config key is proven accepted by real job discovery and schema validation, `validate()` runs against real machines, and the job appears in the outcomes block — which is exactly the class of breakage a config key present in no test config invites.

Do **not** seed their divergences into `seed_a_divergence_in_every_manager` or `seed_a_pending_write_in_every_manager`:

- A sideload seed costs a `snap try` on pc1 plus a snapd install on pc2 (~15–20 s) on the suite's two most expensive runs.

### (e) #263 mark side — verdict

**The three-way answer itself is not integration-testable, and `BOTH` and `SOURCE` are unreachable on a VM by construction.** `_ask_mark_sides` is a `prompt_toolkit` `decision_list` reached only after the interactive per-group loop, and both routes the suite has return earlier: the automation-environment branch returns a `ReviewOutcome` immediately after `_answer_by_policy`, and the no-TTY branch returns before the loop. An unattended run answering a conflicting item `SKIP_ALWAYS` writes the mark to the **target's** decision file and nowhere else, and does not perform the overwrite. That is the behavior every scripted and CI run will actually get, and it currently has no VM proof at all — nor does the conflicting-item class itself.

Deliberately not attempted: the two-file read-back (`_mark_holders` returning `(False, True)` for `CHANGE`, so a mark holds from either direction). It needs a second, reversed sync and its subject is D-08a, not #263. Defer.

## 3. Hardening `tests/unit/test_scenario_coverage_matrix.py`

Three assertions, each closing a *silent* drift path. Specify intent; the executor writes the regex.

**(a) Ids are unique.** `_rows()` builds a `dict[str, …]`, so a second row with a live id overwrites the first and nothing notices — the module docstring already claims "a unique id" and nothing enforces it. Intent: collect ids in document order, record the ones seen twice, and assert on that in `test_the_matrix_is_well_formed` alongside the mark-legend check. Do **not** raise at import: `ROWS`/`CLAIMED` are module-level and an import-time failure kills collection of all 2789 parametrised cases and reports as a collection error rather than as a named assertion. The message's job: name each repeated id, and say that the *earlier* row was never verified — so the fix is to renumber one block, never to delete a row.

**(b) A citation naming a module-level test resolves, and is checked.** `CITATION` requires a `Test…::` class prefix and `BARE_TEST` requires the backtick to sit immediately before `::`, so a `module:::test_x` cell matches neither and is dropped without trace — leaving the row's remaining unit citation to satisfy every check while the `V` half goes unread. Module-level test functions are legal and common here (61 across `tests/`, including in `tests/integration/`), so the form must be *supported*, not banned. Intent: teach the resolver the `<module>:::<test>` shape; extend `_docstrings()`, which today walks only `ClassDef` bodies, to also collect module-level `test_*` functions keyed by their module stem; then `test_every_cited_test_exists` and `test_every_cited_test_names_the_scenario_back` bind to them unchanged. Failure message's job: distinguish "that module has no such module-level test" from "that test exists inside a class, cite it as `Class::test`" — the two mistakes have different fixes. Side benefit: `test_no_test_claims_a_scenario_the_matrix_does_not_have` and the tag-readability check start seeing module-level docstrings, which they never have.

**(c) A `same test` phrase alongside explicit citations must add to them, not be ignored.** `_rows()` consults `SAME_AS` only when `resolved` is empty, so a cell holding both — `C135` — silently keeps the explicit half and discards the inherited one. Intent: when a cell carries a `same test`/`same as` phrase *and* explicit citations, append the inherited citations rather than skipping the branch. Five rows carry both (`C29`, `C121`, `C122`, `C135`, `E55`); the other four inherit citations that exist and the name-back check needs only one citation to match, so only `C135` changes behaviour — which is the point, and C2 is what makes it pass. `C133`/`C134` (whole-cell `same test`) keep working unchanged; verify.

**Explicit non-goal:** do not add "a `V` may only cite one of the three integration modules". The resolver discards the module token today; recording it for every citation to enforce a rule the prose states (line 70) is a larger change than the defect warrants, and none of the 5 broken rows needed it.

## 7. The two staleness stamps

**Re-stamp the coverage doc. Do not fully re-stamp the criteria doc.**

**Coverage, line 70** — "The integration suite last passed whole at `a2c299dc`". This is a claim about a suite run: cheap, verifiable, and it is *load-bearing* here, because C4–C8 add `V` marks and the sentence's second clause ("a `V` added after that commit has not yet run") is the only thing telling a reader which claims are unrun. Re-stamp in C12, **after** the VM suite passes whole on the branch, as the last commit — any later `V` invalidates it. If the suite does not pass whole, leave the old sha: the sentence is already correct for that case and is the honest reading.

**Criteria, line 378** — "Read against the code at `c6e4bf33`; articles untouched since `502321ec` were last read there." Bluffing it is worse than leaving it stale, because the *Where the tool does not yet meet these requirements* section derives its authority from it.

questions.question: The doc audit found real holes. How much of the doc remediation belongs in this PR?

options.label: Tests + matrix fixes (Recommended)
options.description: New/updated integration tests, their mandatory coverage-matrix rows, plus the cross-cutting matrix defects: 12 duplicate scenario IDs (H218-H226, K94-K96), 4 phantom `V` citations the cross-check can't see, hardening test_scenario_coverage_matrix.py, and stale post-job-split rows (K15, N22, K9-K12, K.5 preamble, Legend table).

options.label: Tests + matrix + prose docs
options.description: All of the above plus the requirements/criteria prose: give PKG-FR-APT-TIMER-PAUSE and the 4 PKG-FR-APPLY-FLAGS* articles a home in package-sync-user-requirements.md (they currently have none), amend the two contradicted sentences, and add manual_flatpak_sync to the criteria job roster (line 25).

options.label: Tests only, report docs
options.description: Write only the integration tests plus the coverage rows the cross-check forces, and hand you a written report of every doc hole for a later session.

questions.question: The apt-timer suspension (#260) has zero VM proof, and the VMs deliberately mask apt-daily{,-upgrade}.timer so the code path never runs. Testing it means arming the real timers for one test window.

options.label: Arm in the test (Recommended)
options.description: Test-local: assert apt-daily{,-upgrade}.SERVICE are still masked as an interlock, write Persistent=false drop-ins under /run, unmask+start the timers only, restore mask in finally. No fixtures-version bump. Residual risk of a leaked unmask is bounded — services stay masked, so no apt can run, and the next session's baseline swap clears it.

options.label: Skip the VM timer test
options.description: Leave #260 unit-only (48 mocked rows) and register it in the Gaps section. Saves ~80s CI and all VM risk, but the whole point of #260 — that the self-heal survives a killed run — stays unproven on real systemd.

questions.question: Four rows (F21, F90, F93, F103) claim VM coverage citing flatpak integration tests that never existed. They predate 670c0438, so they're outside what you asked for.

options.label: Demote and register (Recommended)
options.description: Mark them `U`, delete the fake citations, and add them to the Gaps register naming what a VM run would have to assert. Honest and cheap. F103 gets re-cited instead if the existing end-to-end filter assertion already covers it.

options.label: Write the missing tests too
options.description: Add the three flatpak VM tests: remote-provisioned-before-install ordering, one remote name serving two vendors, source filter replication. Costs a Flathub-backed workstream (~3 more syncs, several more CI minutes) on top of the requested scope.

questions.question: The conformance-criteria staleness stamp says every one of its 145 articles was read against c6e4bf33 — an ancestor of 670c0438. None of the 7 PRs' articles have been re-read.

options.label: Leave stamp, note it (Recommended)

options.label: Partial re-stamp (25 articles)
options.description: Re-read against HEAD the 25 articles the 7 PRs touched and add a second stamp tier naming them, keeping c6e4bf33 as the base tier. Roughly a day of careful reading on top of the test work.
